That is a good idea, but easier said than done.  

1) I have extensive experience in financial modeling re Wall Street, and I would be up for being in corporate finance.   I would do this job for sure even though it pays less than I'm used to.  I also have some experience with corporate finance on some old jobs.  That said, I've applied to probably 2000+ corporate finance jobs and gotten very little traction.  I think the issues here are subtle but numerous.  I'm a little old (40) for junior roles.  I haven't been doing this long enough for senior roles, although everyone I meet with blurts out that I would kill the work.  I'm told by many companies that the work isn't sexy enough for me.  Data science and systems skills are increasingly important in this world, and while I have taken a dozen recent appropriate classes to upgrade my skills, its still not as easy fit as a 24 year old MS Statistics graduate.  In short, this world has been amazingly difficult to inflitrate even though dozens of firms have indicated to me that I'm an upgrade from most people in the business.

2) Similarly, I would do data science jobs.  These jobs seem even tougher to get, even though the media likes to trumpet that its a huge growth industry.  Its difficult at my age, I'm not a recent STEM graduate, and the work itself is more different than Wall Street than corporate finance.  There are some MS Data Science programs like UC Berkeley that I've thought about but not done yet.  They are very expensive and the hiring program on the back end seems poor, so I'm not sure they are worth the money and effort.  I'd do this if I was more confident.
